correctness.rationale: The three partials give the unique affine singularity (2,4) over the algebraic closure (Frobenius is injective), and none at infinity. The pencil polynomial is primitive over k[r] since its leading coefficient r+3 and constant −2r² are coprime. Its discriminant r^5(r−3) is nonsquare by odd valuation at r=3, proving irreducibility after inverting u; the excluded lines u=0 and Z=0 are not components. The homogeneous forms give a base-point-free quartic parametrization: W=0 forces s=0, where D is nonzero. The image has degree four and the pullback of a line has degree four, forcing map degree one; the normalization fiber over P is exactly s=0. The cleared-numerator calculations verify orders 2 and 7. In the complete normalized DVR, take a parameter b with u=b² by taking the square root of its unit factor. Subtract the even part of η and divide by its odd part's even unit to obtain b^7 in the completed local ring. The resulting subring k[[b²,b^7]] already has colength three, and the genus formula gives total colength three because P is the only singularity and the normalization is rational. This proves equality, the semigroup, and the conductor b^6. The local-unit quotient for Pic^0 reduces to the finite conductor quotients; truncated log and exp are inverse group morphisms there, also on k-algebra points, since all relevant denominators through degree five are units. The normalized principal-unit space modulo the local subspace has basis represented by b,b³,b^5. Over F7 the only special fiber consists of a single rational point, so normalization gives all stated extension-field point counts.
residual_risks: The bounded reproduction certifies the polynomial identities and order computations only; geometric integrality, unibranchness, the local-unit description and the extension-field count use the proof. No formal verification or expert attestation is claimed.
